response.sql: WITH patient_level AS (SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, AVG(l.ALB) AS avg_alb, AVG(l.UN / l.`T-BIL`) AS avg_ratio FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = l.ID GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX), sex_level AS (SELECT SEX, AVG(avg_alb) AS avg_alb, AVG(avg_ratio) AS avg_ratio FROM patient_level GROUP BY SEX), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_alb) AS mean_alb FROM sex_level) SELECT s.SEX, s.avg_alb, s.avg_ratio, s.avg_alb - o.mean_alb AS alb_above_mean FROM sex_level s CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE s.avg_alb > o.mean_alb;

assumptions.assumption: Lab records are inner-joined to Patient on ID, so unmatched lab rows are dropped. Each patient's ALB average uses all of their lab dates, and their ratio is the average of UN/T-BIL over their lab rows where both values are present and T-BIL is nonzero (SQLite returns NULL for division by zero, and AVG skips NULLs).

The 'mean of the sex-level ALB averages' is the unweighted mean across sex groups that have a non-null average ALB. Each sex group, including NULL and blank SEX, counts equally regardless of patient count.
